description:
MEDIUM AND CONSTRUCTION. Every token is built from the same small vocabulary of flat, hard-edged, semi-transparent filled shapes on a near-black ground (a very dark neutral, not pure black): rotated squares and rectangles, long thin slats or bars, circles, and a scatter of tiny squares and diamonds. No outlines, no strokes, no gradients, no texture, no line work - everything is a filled silhouette. Because the fills are translucent and heavily layered, the overlaps do all the shading: where two or three orange panes cross the colour deepens toward brown; where many stack, the centre goes bright and near-opaque. That layered translucency is the only modelling in the work.

PALETTE. One hue family and nothing else: terracotta / burnt orange at the top end, through mid russet, down to a very dark umber that sits only a step above the ground. No second hue anywhere, no accent, no grey, no white. Value is the only variable - the bright orange slabs read as light, the deep brown squares read as shadow, the black ground reads as void.

SUBJECT. Nothing representational. Each token is a heap: a pile of overlapping panes tossed onto a dark surface, closest to scattered cards, roof slates or plates of glass. A few seeds become more specific - 9190, 10443 and 10980 read as a spoked burst or asterisk, a fistful of long thin sticks thrown down and crossing near a centre; 10801 and 9369 read as a dense mosaic wall; 10622 reads as a handful of large slabs sliding past each other.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. All twelve are centred agglomerations. Each has a mass in the middle of the square frame and, around it, a loose fringe of satellites that are almost always circles. The brightest, largest, most opaque pieces sit at or near the centre; the darkest browns sit behind or outside. In almost every neutral token the corners of the frame are empty. The compositional template is fixed: centred heap, circular fringe, empty corners, no use of the frame edge.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Density: 10443 and 9011 are sparse and mostly ground; 9548, 9369, 10801 and 10264 are dense and nearly fill the tile. Dominant primitive: 9190, 9906, 10443 and 10980 are bar-dominated with long diagonal slats; 10622 is slab-dominated with a few very large rectangles; 10801 is circle-dominated with a heavy ring of discs; 9011 and 10085 are small-confetti-dominated. Scale: 10622's pieces are several times the size of 10443's. Silhouette: radial burst (10443, 9190) vs ragged blobby mass (9548, 9727) vs vertical column (9190, 9906) vs squared block (10801). These are differences of gesture, not just rotations of one arrangement.

THE THREE STATES. Neutral is the tight version: the heap is compact, the centre bright and opaque, the satellites close in, the frame edges clear. Stress dilates it - the same elements pull apart, spacing opens, far more black shows between them, the bright opaque core shrinks or breaks up, the proportion of dark umber shapes rises, and elements migrate outward until they reach and cross the tile edge (in 9369 stress and 9548 stress the outermost circles and squares are cut by the boundary). The impression is of an object blown apart and gone colder. Recovery re-gathers it: the core returns bright and large, the satellites close back in, but it does not return to the neutral arrangement - recovery is consistently a little looser and a little heavier in dark discs than neutral, so the three states read as a cycle rather than a two-state toggle.

IDENTITY ACROSS STATES. Same seed, three states, is still recognisably one token. 9011 keeps its single hard-edged bright pentagonal core in all three. 9190 keeps its crossed diagonal sticks. 9369 keeps the big central pane with a disc ring beneath it. 9548 keeps its ragged multi-armed mass. The rearrangement is large but the character and the dominant primitive are preserved throughout.

AT 120PX. The state change is clearly visible at browse size - the stress row is obviously airier, darker and more scattered than the neutral row for all four seeds shown, so the market response survives reduction. Seed identity survives less evenly. 10443 (thin star), 10622 (big slabs), 10801 (disc-heavy block), 9190 and 9906 (diagonal bars) and 9011 (small and sparse) are each immediately distinguishable. But 9369, 9548, 9727, 10085 and 10264 collapse at 120 into much the same thing: an irregular orange blob with a fringe of dots. Checked against the 256 sheet, the detail is genuinely present in those five - distinct pane arrangements - it simply is not carrying to thumbnail size. Roughly half the set reads as individual works at browse size and half reads as one recurring stamp.

ARTIFACTS. Clipping: several tokens have circles and squares cut by the tile boundary, most visibly in the stress row (9369, 9548) and at neutral in 9369 and 10801 where discs are sliced by the top and bottom edges. It reads as a bounding-box crop rather than a deliberate bleed, because the cut shapes are ordinary satellites rather than composed elements. Mush: in the densest seeds (9548, 9369, 10264) the centre stacks so many translucent panes that it saturates into a flat opaque orange field with no readable structure inside it - the layering stops contributing and simply fills. Muddiness: in the 512 single, the many-layer overlaps through the middle go a dull dark brown that is neither the bright orange nor the black, and it is the least resolved part of the image.
